chunks: From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafsa ibn Suqat, from the one he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who plays with his wife or his female slave while he is in the makeup (qada) of the month of Ramadan, and semen precedes him causing ejaculation, he said: 'Upon him is the expiation like that of the one who has intercourse in Ramadan.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: 'We have already discussed a similar report previously, so there is no need to repeat it.'

key_terms.قَضَاءُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Makeup of the month of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for ejaculating during sexual play while making up Ramadan fasts?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes that pre-seminal emission (surbah) during sexual play in the days of Qada (make-up) Ramadan incurs the same major expiation (kaffarah) as full intercourse, highlighting the juristic consensus on the equivalence of acts breaking the fast regardless of the specific month. The note by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan indicates this ruling is well-established in Shia fiqh, often cited alongside the primary evidence from Surah Al-Baqarah. This ruling underscores the seriousness of breaking the fast through sexual intimacy, even in its preliminary stages, during the sacred month.
